doc.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018

title: What makes a good accompanist
summary: A good accompanist breathes with the singer and leaves space; she tells a story of a guitarist who gave her none.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Because people get jaded, you know I think, how could you, right? But some people do. So now you’re in a position, when you do your solo gigs like tonight, you’re the leader. I want to talk about accompanists for a minute. For you what makes a good accompanist?

A person that listens and breathes along with you, breathes along with the singer so that we are one. So I would say through — going through a series of musicians to find people who were into swing and blues and the kind of stuff that I like to do, I found artists that are aligned, that we feel the same way. Our pocket is the same. We swing the same. We play the blues the same. So that’s what I look for is just alignment in thinking. And people that leave space. Because I have experienced working with guitar players, I mean throughout the years of jamming in clubs and things like that when they, “Catherine come up and sing these blues.” So I’d get up and sing something and the guys don’t leave me any space. So there was one night I remember where he’s a nice person, sweet, I still know him today, but I wouldn’t finish a phrase and he’d be [scats]. And so I just put the mic down. I said — obviously you have more to say than I do.

Well he didn’t know. You know, he didn’t know. And it wasn’t my gig. I didn’t call him for the gig it was just a bunch of us who were jamming. So you go through a lot of different situations with different musicians to find the people who you are aligned with the most.
Do you ever sort of like someone but they’re doing something that you think you can change them some? Is it worth the potential?

That’s tough you know. Some people take constructive — it’s not criticism, but can we do it like this. Some people take that personally. Like, “I’m not doing — why? Aren’t I don’t a good job?” type of thing. So it depends. If I want to go through that with the person, because the other 99 percent of what they’re doing is great, then I’ll try to do that. I’ll try to work and say, “Can we arrive at this?” It depends. So as I say, if the other 99 percent of what they’re doing is working for me then I will try to mold that and get it to where I want it or I’ll drop it and deal with somebody else.
